content:
Apple TV's brand new original comedy series "Brothers" will premiere next month, starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. Here's the trailer.

The comedy series "Brothers" will debut on September 23, created by Lee Eisenberg of "The Office" fame.

Apple TV is currently airing the fourth season of "Ted Lasso," but another highly anticipated comedy is about to arrive.

"Brothers," starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, is a brand new original series in which they play fictionalized versions of themselves.

"Brothers" will premiere on September 23 (Wednesday) with its first two episodes available immediately, followed by weekly releases until the season finale on November 4.

The series is showrun by Lee Eisenberg, who was a key creative force behind the beloved sitcom "The Office," serving as a writer and producer during seasons 2 through 6.

Below is the synopsis provided by Apple for "Brothers," followed by the trailer:

Joining "Brothers" on Apple TV in September are: a new season of "Slow Horses," the original crime thriller "Last Seen," and the Ryan Reynolds-led film "Mayday."

What did you think of the "Brothers" trailer? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, with discounts available through Apple One bundles.
